draft.title: The first farmers
card: For most of human history, people moved around to hunt animals and gather wild plants. Farming began when people started to grow crops and keep animals for food.
Crops and herds stay in one place, so farming families could settle near their fields. Over time, small groups of homes grew into villages.
Farmers could often grow more food than their families needed. This extra food is called a surplus, and it could be stored or traded.
With a surplus, not everyone had to spend their days finding food. Some people could become potters, toolmakers or traders.
draft.remember: Farming let people settle, and a food surplus let some people do other work.

a.q: Why did farming lead some people to take up new jobs such as pottery?
opts: A food surplus meant not everyone had to produce food
Farmers had to move often, so they needed new tools
Hunting animals became easier once crops were grown
Villages were too small for everyone to farm
a.why: A surplus meant the farmers could feed people who did not grow food, so some could make pots or tools. Farming tied people to their fields, so moving often is not the reason.
a.clue: Think about what extra food made possible.

b.q: Long ago, a group of hunter-gatherers in the hills began planting barley and keeping goats near a river. Which change is most likely to follow in the years after?
opts: They build permanent homes near their fields
They travel further each season to find wild food
They stop needing to store or trade any food
They give up their tools because farming is simple
b.why: Crops and goats need daily care in one place, so settling near the fields is the likely result. Travelling further to find wild food is the old way of life that farming replaced.
b.clue: Crops cannot follow the people around.

a.best: A food surplus meant not everyone had to produce food

b.best: They build permanent homes near their fields

problems.detail: "Crops and herds stay in one place" is not true of herds. Herding peoples (pastoral nomads) often moved their animals from place to place. Only crops tie people to one spot, so the line should be about crops, or say that herds kept near fields can stay in one place.
The why says "Crops and goats need daily care in one place". Goats can be herded from place to place, so it is the barley crop that ties the group to the river. The why should rest on the crops.

check.summary: Both questions are sound and have one clear answer. The card and the why for (b) wrongly say herds or goats must stay in one place, when only crops tie people to their fields.
